First, we complete the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-10{x}^{2}+40x-27 \\  & =-10({x}^{2}-4x)-27 \\  & =-10(({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2})-{2}^{2})-27 \\  & =-10((x-2)^{2}-4)-27 \\  & =-10{(x-2)}^{2}+40-27 \\  & =-10{(x-2)}^{2}+13\end{aligned}
$$

    

To find the inverse of a function, we follow these steps:

**Step 1:** Replace $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=-10{(x-2)}^{2}+13
$$

**Step 2:** Swap $x$ and $y:$

$$
x=-10{(y-2)}^{2}+13
$$

**Step 3:** Solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-10{(y-2)}^{2}+13 \\ 10{(y-2)}^{2} & =13-x \\ (y-2)^{2} & =\frac{13-x}{10} \\ y-2 & =-\sqrt{\frac{13-x}{10}} \\ y & =2-\sqrt{\frac{13-x}{10}}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we selected the negative square root because if the domain of $f(x)$ is $x\le 2,$ then the range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ is  ${f}^{-1}\le 2.$

**Step 4:** Replace $y$ with ${f}^{-1}(x):$

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=2-\sqrt{\frac{13-x}{10}}
$$
